name: Rainbow Countdown Sticker
tagline: The app's rainbow timer, die-cut like one of its own stickers: the time already spent is simply cut away.
concept: This takes the widget every class watches and makes it one of the app's own stickers. The thick, round-capped rainbow countdown ring circles a clean, empty cream face, wrapped in the stickers' thick white die-cut border. Because a die-cut follows its artwork, the 110° of time already spent at the upper-left is cut out of the sticker, leaving only the border and the widget's thin track hugging the face through the gap. That notch does the numeral's job: the silhouette itself says "countdown in progress", it stays closed so it never reads as a C, a spinner or a refresh arrow, its ends are fat round caps wrapped in border (the opposite of an arrowhead), and the arc starts at 12 o'clock exactly like the widget's. The colours are the app's own: the six hues of the in-app rainbow sticker, deepened to crayon enamel with crisp flat joins so it reads as a printed object rather than a glowing AI halo, sitting on the amber canvas reduced to two flat facets with a cream edge; the spent track is the brand's pale sage, and the dark variant turns the face charcoal and the track deep sage, the way the widget's dark mode does. The glyph is literally the sticker's outline with the face knocked out, scaled 1.48×, so its hole, thin section, notch depth and cap bumps match the colour icon in proportion. In the menu bar it can run live: the notch widens counter-clockwise as the arc shrinks back toward 12, until only the thin ring is left at "Time's up".
glyphNotes: At 18px, and at true 1x 16px (where the 256-unit hole and the 64-unit thin section land on whole pixels), it reads as a heavy ring with a clear bite out of its upper-left, closed by a 1px ring, so it never becomes an open C or an arrow. The silhouette is the colour sticker's die-cut outline with the face knocked out: one solid #000 even-odd path with round, filleted caps.

name: Rainbow Rider
tagline: The app's own hamster rides the leading end of the rainbow timer ring and runs the countdown down, just as it does on the classroom board.
concept: This is the master timer ring with a clean face. The app's own calm hamster rides its leading cap at 7 o'clock. The hamster is the verbatim creatures.tsx markup, placed with CreatureAnimation's runner transform (rotate about the ring centre, translate to the runner radius, scale(k,−k)), so it runs counter-clockwise inside the wheel with its feet on the track. It is mirrored exactly as the widget shows it on the lower half of the ring, with the rainbow still ahead of it and the pale spent track behind. With no numeral, the ring itself carries the identity. A closed die-cut rim plus a heavy arc that visibly ends under a small animal cannot pass for a spinner, a refresh arrow, goforward.5 or the letter C/G. The six bands are crisp crayon colours from the app's sticker rainbow with short joins rather than a glowing gradient, which avoids the AI-halo look. Colour is the app's real vernacular: the rainbow ring, the cream widget face and the hamster's own #D2691E/#DEB887/#8B4513, all on the amber canvas plate with its cream edge and just two large facets. The dark variant relights the plate and face to charcoal so the orange hamster glows. The small master is the same drawing flattened into six hard bands, with heavier hamster outlines. The glyph is the icon with colour removed at identical proportions: a 64-unit closed rim stands for the die-cut edge and spent track, and a 160-unit arc stands for rim plus rainbow band (34% of the radius in both), with the hamster's silhouette fused onto the leading cap. Live in the menu bar, the arc shortens while the hamster rides its end once round the ring (upside-down across the top, as in the widget) until only the outline is left.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as a closed ring, heavy on the right and bottom, with a solid lump sitting where the arc ends. At @2x the lump resolves into the hamster's round head, two ears and an eye hole over its back hump, with its feet sunk into the arc. It is one #000 evenodd path: the rim is 64 units, the arc 160 and the eye hole 66, so every stroke and counter meets the 64-unit minimum (the ears are low bumps on the head, not strokes).

name: Gold Star Finish
tagline: The rainbow timer every class watches, set and ready, with the app's gold star sticker slapped on its 12 o'clock finish line.
concept: This is the master rainbow ring with one gold star sticker on it. The ring has a flat six-colour arc with round caps, an empty cream face, a white die-cut rim, and an amber plate with two large facets and a cream edge. The star is chunky and drawn like the app's own stickers: a thick white border, a soft shadow and an 8° tilt. It is about a quarter of the ring's width and sits in the ring's gap at 12 o'clock, where the app's countdown starts and its spent gap opens, so the icon reads as "the timer, and a gold star when time's up". I moved the star from mid-gap at 10:30 to 12 o'clock for two reasons. In testing, a blob at 10:30 on an open ring read as a reload arrowhead at 16–36 px, and a C with a star in its mouth is the star-and-crescent (☪) risk flagged in round 2. At 12 o'clock the mark is symmetric, so it has no arrow direction. The pale sage spent track also closes the ring, so it cannot read as a C, a loading spinner or a power symbol. The colours stay true to the app. The rainbow blocks are flat with hard joins, so the ring reads as an object rather than an AI halo. The warm gold star sits between the red and violet caps, well away from the yellow segment. Cream and white are the widget surfaces, and the track uses a pale sage from the brand palette. The glyph is the icon with the colour removed. The rainbow becomes a solid thick arc and the pale track becomes a 72-unit line that closes the ring, with fillets where it meets the caps. The sticker becomes a solid star 126 units clear of both caps. The dark variant and the 16–32 px master are the same drawing, re-lit and simplified. There is no numeral and no hamster. In the live menu-bar state, the arc shortens counter-clockwise from the star exactly as the app's ring does, so the familiar upper-left spent gap opens beside the star. At zero, only the star is left on its track.
glyphNotes: At a true 18 px the glyph reads as a closed ring with a small crown on top, which looks like a stopwatch rather than a reload arrow, a power symbol or the letter C. At 36 px (18 pt @2x) the crown resolves into the five-point star. The silhouette is one filleted outline, a thick round-capped arc that flows into a 72-unit spent track, plus the solid star. It is all #000, and nothing is thinner than 64 units.

name: Rainbow Block Dial
tagline: The rainbow timer every class watches, rebuilt as six chunky toy blocks: five lit, one already spent, and nothing in the middle.
concept: The app's signature timer rebuilt as a toy: the cream face and white die-cut rim teachers watch every lesson, ringed by six chunky soft-cornered blocks that run clockwise from twelve in the stickers' own rainbow (thumbs-up pink, star orange, lemon, green, periwinkle), with the last, violet block at 10–12 o'clock already used up and left as an empty recessed socket, so the ring tells the countdown and the face stays clean, with no numeral and no mascot. Without a numeral, the identity has to come from the ring itself: flat blocks with narrow seams answer the AI-halo and Google One risks (no gradient glow, no digit, and deliberately not Google's red-yellow-green-blue quartet), and because the spent slot is drawn as an empty socket rather than an open gap, the silhouette is a closed dial that cannot read as a C, a refresh arrow, goforward.5 or a spinner's fading tail. The amber canvas plate keeps only two large flat facets plus a cream keyline so it lifts off the amber board, depth comes from soft warm grey-green shadows under the blocks, and the dark appearance keeps the rainbow while turning the face charcoal and the rim taupe on a deeper amber plate. The glyph is the same six-slot drawing with colour removed (five solid blocks plus the spent block as a 64-unit hollow outline, seams opened to 104 units for 16px), and it can run live in the menu bar: all six blocks fill when a timer starts, one hollows out counterclockwise from 11 o'clock with each sixth of the time, and the ring blinks at zero.
glyphNotes: A closed ring of five heavy soft-cornered blocks with the sixth, at 11 o'clock, drawn as a hollow outline: a countdown dial with one slot spent, not a C, an arrow or a spinner arc. At 18pt @2x the hollow slot and the 3.7px seams are crisp; at true 1x 16px the seams stay 1.6px open and the spent block drops to a lighter outline, so it still reads as six distinct blocks.

name: Sage Countdown Sticker
tagline: The app's own die-cut timer ring, spent time cut away, re-voiced in the calm brand palette: dusty rose, terracotta, amber and sage on deep sage.
concept: Sage Countdown is the master ring's exact drawing re-voiced for a client who liked the shipping icon's calm palette: the app's cream timer face, left empty (no numeral, no hamster), inside a thick round-capped band, die-cut like one of the app's stickers so the spent upper-left section is simply cut away and the white border hugs the face around the widget's thin grey track. The band keeps the timer's own rainbow order but speaks it in brand enamel, dusty rose at twelve o'clock through terracotta, the amber of the app's canvas and sage to a deep sage-teal leading cap, blended in OKLCH through a pistachio waypoint so it never turns khaki, and drawn as one continuous opaque sweep because muted colour blocks read as a dashboard donut chart (and a red-yellow-green trio drifts toward the Chrome logo). It sits on a deep sage plate with two large flat facets, the one brand colour against which the white die-cut and its cut-away notch read on light app grids, dark docks and the amber board alike, and the sweep deliberately ends lighter than the plate so the band's tail is never mistaken for more spent gap. Identity without a numeral comes from the ring itself: the silhouette steps down exactly where time is spent, the thin track keeps the form closed so it cannot read as a C, a loading spinner or a refresh arrow, and the oversized round knob caps are never arrowheads; the glyph is that same sticker silhouette with the face knocked out, byte-for-byte the master ring's glyph, so choosing the calm palette changes nothing in the menu bar, and in a live menu-bar state the band retracts counter-clockwise toward twelve as a timer runs until only the closed thin ring is left at Time's Up. Dark appearance deepens the plate to near-black green, tones the sticker to grey, lifts the sweep and turns the face into the app's own dark-mode timer face (warm-gray-800), and the small master flattens the same die-cut onto a full-bleed deep sage square with the border and band thickened on the 64-unit grid and the sweep simplified to fewer stops.
glyphNotes: At 18px, and at true 16px on a 100%-scaling school PC, it reads as a heavy ring (band about 3.5 px) that steps down at the upper-left to a closed 1 px track with a round knob at each step: a timer partly run down, not a C, a spinner or a refresh arrow. The silhouette is the die-cut timer sticker itself with the face as the hole, one even-odd #000 path whose thinnest part is 64 units, identical to the master ring's glyph.
direction: The ring in the brand palette

name: Hamster at Home
tagline: The timer's own hamster, at home in the rainbow ring where the countdown number used to be.
concept: This is Classroom Widgets' signature timer with the numeral replaced by the creature that runs around it. The app's own calm hamster (the exact creatures.tsx markup under one transform, not redrawn) sits large and centred on the cream face, and the ring drains the way the real one does: a 250° round-capped arc from twelve o'clock, with the pale spent track open at the upper-left. The ring uses the six flat bands of the app's rainbow sticker (#ff4444 to #8844ff, lightly deepened) with hard joins, so it reads as a sticker-bright timer rather than a smooth glowing AI halo; it sits in a white die-cut rim on the real amber canvas plate (top-left light, two large facets, soft warm shadows) with a cream outline that separates it from the board, and dark appearance re-lights it as the app's actual dark timer (warm-gray-800 face, warm-gray-700 track, deeper plate, no glare). With no digit, the hamster carries the identity: an eared animal standing inside an open ring can't be read as a spinner, refresh arrow, letter C or numeral-in-ring badge, and both caps stay round. The glyph is the same drawing without colour — the same arc and the hamster at the same place and scale, reduced to one solid sign (round head with two round ears pushed just outside the outline, oval body, two stubby paws, curly tail, two eye knockouts) held 100 units clear of the ring; the small master flattens the same composition to five bands with heavier outlines on a 32-unit grid; and as a live menu-bar state the arc shortens from its tail back toward twelve in step with a running timer until only the hamster is left.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as a small eared animal standing inside an open, round-capped ring. The ring is 104 units wide, the hamster sits 100 units clear of it, and every feature is at least 64 units (ears pushed out of the head, two 84-unit eyes with a 70-unit bridge, paws with a 69-unit gap, a 70-unit tail), so the ears and paws stop it collapsing into a ghost or blob at true 16px and the eyes are crisp at 36px. The silhouette is the app hamster reduced to a sign: round head with two round ears at the front-left, oval body, two stubby paws and the curly tail, facing left as it runs on the timer.

name: The Reel
tagline: The name picker every class watches, caught the instant the reel lands on one name.
concept: The Reel freezes the randomiser the instant it lands. The app's own cream card and lilac→orchid→pink→peach→butter slot window (stops sampled from the widget) hold the chosen name chip, bright white in the middle, with its faded, foreshortened neighbours cropped by the window edge above and below like a drum that has just stopped. It is one centred object at 71% of the plate width that stays inside the 80% maskable circle, on the amber board with a cream rim so it separates from the real canvas, plus only two flat paper flecks in the app's confetti yellow and navy on a counter-diagonal (chosen over red and teal because they differ from amber in brightness). There are no digits, no letters and no hamster: the chip holds only the dark shape of a bold name in the app's near-black ink, because a blank chip read as a toggle or search field last round, and removing that one element leaves the chip truly empty if the client prefers. Identity comes from the reel's hierarchy rather than a ring: one solid pill between two smaller outlined pills inside a closed frame says "pick one", the near-square, nub-free frame keeps clear of the battery slab, and leaving the flecks out of the glyph avoids the toaster/face reading that sank round 2's slot. Icon and glyph are the same drawing (card edge → frame, white chip → solid pill, white-rimmed neighbours → outline pills); the dark variant re-lights those parts on a deep caramel plate, the small master keeps only amber, cream, the sweep, the white chip, two neighbour stubs and a hairline name on a 32-unit grid, and in the menu bar the three pills can roll upward through the frame while a pick spins, with the middle one snapping solid on landing.
glyphNotes: At 18pt it reads as a rounded, near-square frame holding one bold solid pill between two smaller outlined pills: a "selected row" sign in one solid tone, built from an 84-unit frame and 64-unit outlines, with no flecks and no opacity. At true 1x 16px the outlines soften into dimmer bars around the bright centre (the way the app fades the neighbours), and the square, nub-free frame keeps it from reading as the battery beside it.

name: Ring & Signal
tagline: The rainbow timer every class watches, with the classroom traffic light docked at its side: two real widgets, one mark, and nothing inside.
concept: The mark is two of the app's own widgets. The rainbow timer ring is the hero, and its cream face is left empty on purpose: no numeral and no hamster. The classroom traffic light (the toolbar's Traffic Light widget) is the one supporting accent, tucked into the ring's right flank like a docked panel. That tells the "widgets, plural" story without a collage, and both objects fit inside the 80% maskable circle (ring reaches radius 288, pill 329 of 330). With no numeral, the identity comes from the ring itself. It uses the timer's actual gradient from timer.tsx, a left-to-right sweep, so the round start cap at 12 o'clock is green, the right side runs cyan to blue to violet, the lower-left turns yellow and orange, and the end cap at the 80° spent gap is red. Add the app's grey spent track at upper-left and the pill biting into the band, and no spinner, refresh arrow, C, G or Google One ring looks like this. Colour: an amber board plate with two large facets and a cream keyline so it stands apart on the app's own amber canvas, sticker-white die-cut rims on both objects, and the traffic light in the app's gray-800→900 with only the green "discuss" lamp lit, echoing the green start cap. The dark variant uses the app's warm-gray-800 dark-mode face, toned rims and a deep caramel plate, and the small master flattens everything onto a 32-unit grid with all three lamps readable. The glyph is the icon with the colour taken out: the rainbow band becomes a 128-unit arc, the white rims become a 64-unit moat that notches the ring exactly where the pill sits, and the pill keeps three knocked-out lamps. It can also go live in the menu bar: the arc shrinks back toward 12 o'clock as a timer runs while the pill stays put as the anchor, and the pill can show only the active lamp open when a Traffic Light widget is on.
glyphNotes: The silhouette is an open C-ring (80° spent gap at upper-left, round caps, no arrowhead) with a small upright traffic-light pill, 3×7 px at 16 px, locked into a notch on its right flank; nothing on the way out is thinner than 64 units. Every edge sits on the 64-unit grid, so at true 16 px and 32 px the three lamps are single crisp knocked-out pixels. At 18pt it reads as timer plus traffic light: crisp at @2x, and at @1x the lamps soften into a dotted pill while the ring-and-pill outline still holds.

name: Die-cut Timer
tagline: The rainbow timer every class watches, printed as one of the app's own die-cut stickers and slapped on the amber board, with nothing on its face.
concept: The hero is the app's signature timer drawn the way the app draws its stickers: the cream face and round-capped rainbow ring are cut out with a thick white die-cut border, dropped onto the amber board with the stickers' soft down-right shadow and turned 15° (the app tilts stickers in 5° steps). That puts the start cap at 12:30, so it reads as slapped on rather than as a clock, and the face stays empty, as the client asked. With no numeral, identity comes from the ring itself: the spent gap sits upper-left, where the real ring drains first, bounded by two round caps and closed off by the die-cut edge, so the mark is always a closed sticker and never an open C, spinner or refresh arrow. The ring is printed in the rainbow sticker's six flat inks (#ff4444 to #8844ff, deepened so the yellow holds against white) as hard-edged bands rather than a smooth glow, which keeps it clear of the AI-halo look; it sits on a two-facet amber plate (#cc8f3d to #8d5428) whose cream rim separates it from the app's own canvas, and the dark variant turns the face and track the app's dark-mode warm charcoal but keeps a toned-down die-cut rim so it still reads as a sticker. The glyph is the same drawing at 1.5× in one tone (same roughly 16/34/50 band/ring/face proportions, same 105° gap and 15° tilt): the die-cut band and the remaining ring merge into one solid shape while the face and spent track are knocked out, and in the menu bar the thick ring drains counterclockwise into the thin outline as a timer runs, leaving just the empty sticker outline at zero. The same white die-cut outline, soft shadow and 5°-step tilt then become the brand's style for web, docs and marketing, where every widget is shown as a sticker.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as a bold closed ring, about 4px thick through the right and bottom, that thins to a 1.4px die-cut line across a round-ended bite at the upper-left (the spent time), around an 8px open face. Because the silhouette is a disc with a hole, it stays closed down to true 16px, so it can't become a C, spinner or refresh arrow, and it sits lighter than a solid badge next to Wi-Fi and battery.
